Backend & Full-Stack Engineer | Node.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL

Gothenburg, Sweden | +46 70 555 0808 | oskar.hl@example.com
GitHub: oskarhl-example | Blog: oskar-codes.example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Full-stack engineer with professional web development experience since 2014, strongest in frontend and experienced building and maintaining production backend services with Node.js, TypeScript, NestJS and Express. Hands-on experience with PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Docker, AWS deployments, automated testing and CI/CD. Contributed to production reliability through on-call work, backend migrations and performance improvements. Fluent in English. Python experience is currently limited to small personal Home Assistant integrations.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Backend: Node.js, NestJS, Express, REST APIs, PHP, Laravel; GraphQL BFF maintenance (Apollo Server)
Databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, Firebase; Prisma, TypeORM
Cloud and delivery: AWS (ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS, CloudWatch, RDS), Docker, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Terraform (modifying existing files), Linux
Testing and observability: Jest, Playwright, Cypress, React Testing Library, Supertest, Sentry, Datadog
Frontend: TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Next.js, Angular, AngularJS, Vue, React Native, HTML, CSS, SCSS
Other: Python (basic; personal projects), Figma, Jira, Confluence, Unleash, Agile/Scrum, BankID

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Full-Stack Developer | Älvgrind Fintech AB | Gothenburg
2021–Present
- Build and maintain onboarding services and customer-facing flows using React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL and AWS in a six-person cross-functional team.
- Designed and implemented a BankID identity verification flow, including QR-code and same-device flows, error handling and retries. A/B tested with 10% of traffic before full rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%.
- Built a secure document-upload service using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning in Lambda, and SQS and PostgreSQL to track scan status.
- Contributed to an incremental migration of the onboarding backend from Express to NestJS, migrating route by route behind the same API gateway.
- Improved mobile Largest Contentful Paint from 4.1 seconds to 1.9 seconds through code splitting, image optimisation and dependency replacement; also migrated the frontend from Create React App to Vite.
- Implemented accessibility audit fixes for the onboarding flow against WCAG 2.1 AA.
- Work with PostgreSQL and Prisma; maintain a GraphQL BFF with another developer. Contribute to automated testing with Jest and Playwright and delivery through GitHub Actions and Docker.
- Participate in the on-call rota, one week every six weeks. Interviewed approximately 30 candidates.
- Acted as team lead for four months in 2024, supporting 1:1s and sprint planning while the team lead was on parental leave.
- The onboarding team received the internal Customer Impact Award in 2023.

Developer | Sjöbris Digital Agency AB | Gothenburg
2018–2021
- Delivered websites and web applications for approximately 25 clients across retail, ferry transport, municipalities and sport.
- Built client applications with Angular, React and Vue, and backend services with Node.js/Express and PHP/Laravel.
- Served as project tech lead and built most of a two-developer React Native ferry-ticket app for purchasing and viewing tickets offline; the app reached approximately 50,000 downloads. The other developer built the payment backend.
- Developed custom WordPress themes and plugins and worked with MySQL, MongoDB and Firebase.
- Set up GitLab CI for the agency, replacing a manual FTP-based deployment process.

Web Developer | Nordkust Media AB | Gothenburg
2014–2018
- Developed newspaper websites and an article editor using PHP, jQuery and AngularJS.
- Implemented a paywall integration and worked with MySQL, Varnish caching and Ubuntu server administration.

Freelance Web Developer / Student
2012–2014
- Built websites for friends, family, a local bakery and two bands using PHP, jQuery and WordPress.

SELECTED PROJECTS
Home Assistant Integrations | Personal | 2022–Present
- Built two small custom home-automation integrations, published on GitHub with approximately 40 stars combined.
- Technologies: Python (basic), YAML.

EDUCATION
Bachelor in Computer Science | West Coast University College (Högskola), Gothenburg | 2011–2014
Graduated 2014.

Additional learning: Advanced React Patterns (2022); AWS Cloud Practitioner course (2020, no exam taken).

LANGUAGES
Swedish: Native | English: Fluent (work language) | Arabic: Spoken at home; limited writing | German: School level

Speaker, local JavaScript meetup (2022): “Migrating Express to NestJS without stopping the world”
Coding bootcamp mentor, Gothenburg (2019–2020)
Driving licence: B
References available on request

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible and well-structured CV with clear chronology, measurable achievements and good technical specificity. The BankID conversion improvement, document-upload architecture, LCP reduction, migration work, on-call participation and ferry-app downloads provide useful evidence of impact. The document is professional and substantially clearer than the original candidate information. The main content limitation is role positioning: it presents the candidate as a full-stack engineer whose strongest area is frontend, while the target role is primarily Python backend engineering. The explicit statement that Python experience is limited is truthful but makes the mismatch especially visible. Some claims could also be made more precise, such as specifying AWS ECS/Fargate rather than only AWS.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, conventional reverse chronology, readable text formatting and relevant ATS keywords including Node.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Docker, AWS, Jest, GitHub Actions and CI/CD. It should parse reliably and has a reasonable AI-screening probability for a comparable-language backend role. Screening probability for this particular Python role is moderate rather than high because Python, FastAPI, Kafka, Kubernetes and the database-specific terms query tuning and schema migrations are not supported by the candidate information. The skills section is keyword-rich without apparent unsupported technologies, although backend, databases, cloud and testing keywords should be given greater prominence than frontend technologies for this application.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate demonstrates more than three years of professional backend experience in a comparable language through Node.js, NestJS and Express, plus solid PostgreSQL, REST, Docker, AWS, automated testing and CI/CD experience. English is clearly shown. The document also supports relevant operational signals: on-call work, production reliability improvements, incremental backend migration and technical knowledge sharing through a meetup talk. However, the candidate does not have three years of professional Python experience, and the source material does not establish willingness to work mainly in Python. Query tuning and live-data PostgreSQL schema migrations are not evidenced. Kafka, Kubernetes and the listed observability platforms Prometheus/Grafana/OpenTelemetry are not evidenced, although Sentry and Datadog provide related observability experience. The candidate does have transport-domain exposure through a ferry ticketing application. Dutch and French are not listed. Overall, this is a credible comparable-language backend application, but not a close match to a Python-first shipment-tracking role.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the opening emphasis on “strongest in frontend” with a truthful backend-focused formulation that foregrounds the comparable-language experience relevant to this role. For example: “Full-stack engineer with 12 years of web development experience, including production backend services with Node.js, TypeScript, NestJS and Express. Experienced with PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Docker, AWS deployments, automated testing, CI/CD and on-call operations.” Keep the truthful Python limitation as a short final sentence if desired, but do not imply professional Python or FastAPI experience.
2. In the Älvgrind Fintech experience section, change “AWS” to “AWS ECS/Fargate, S3, Lambda, SQS and CloudWatch” where those technologies are relevant. This makes the cloud-deployment experience more explicit and uses the job advertisement’s terminology without overstating ownership of the underlying AWS infrastructure.
3. In the Älvgrind experience section, make the REST/backend evidence more explicit by revising the migration bullet to: “Contributed to an incremental migration of production Node.js REST backend services from Express to NestJS, migrating routes behind the same API gateway.” Only use “REST” here because REST is listed in the candidate’s original skills and the work concerns backend routes/API services.
4. In the Technical Skills section, reorder the categories so “Backend,” “Databases,” “Cloud and delivery,” and “Testing and observability” appear before “Frontend.” This better targets the backend role while preserving the candidate’s full-stack profile.

MINOR ATS AND CLARITY IMPROVEMENTS
5. In the Technical Skills section, change “Terraform (modifying existing files)” to “Terraform (small changes to existing configuration)” to preserve the important scope limitation while making the keyword easier to parse.
6. In the Professional Summary or Technical Skills section, use the exact phrase “CI/CD” alongside the existing GitHub Actions and GitLab CI references. For example: “CI/CD: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI.” The current wording implies CI/CD but does not present the exact phrase as prominently as the job advertisement.
7. In the Älvgrind experience section, retain the on-call bullet and consider revising it to “Participate in a one-week-in-six on-call rota for production onboarding services.” This aligns more directly with the target team’s operational-reliability expectations without claiming incident post-mortems or runbook ownership.
8. Remove “References available on request” from the Additional section unless an application system specifically requests it; it uses valuable space without strengthening the evidence for this role.

The employment chronology is clear, the education section is correctly placed before professional experience, and the document presents the candidate's frontend/backend balance honestly. The main content limitation is role fit: the CV clearly presents a strong Node.js/TypeScript backend profile, but it does not establish the database query-tuning or schema-migration experience requested by the role, and Python remains limited to personal projects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly overall: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience, plain text contact details, and recognizable technology names. Keyword coverage is strong for Node.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Docker, AWS, automated testing, GitHub Actions, CI/CD-related tools, on-call work, and observability through Sentry and Datadog. Do not add FastAPI, Kafka, Kubernetes, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, EDI, or database query tuning/schema migrations because these are not supported by the candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate is a credible comparable-language backend candidate. The CV shows more than three years of professional backend development using Node.js, NestJS, Express, PostgreSQL, REST-related services, Docker, AWS, automated testing, CI/CD tooling, and on-call operations. It also shows transport-related experience through the ferry-ticket application, although that is not the same as shipment tracking, logistics platforms, or EDI. The candidate's production-reliability experience, incremental backend migration, on-call participation, measurable performance work, and technical meetup presentation align well with the company's ownership and reliability culture. However, the candidate does not have three years of professional Python experience, and the supplied material does not demonstrate willingness to work mainly in Python. Query tuning and live-data schema migrations are also not evidenced. Kafka or another event-streaming platform, Kubernetes, and Dutch or French are not present. Terraform, observability tooling, and transport-domain exposure are present in partial or adjacent form: Terraform is limited to modifying existing files, observability is represented by Sentry and Datadog rather than the named tools, and transport exposure comes from a ferry application.

2. In the Professional Experience section under Älvgrind Fintech AB, revise the first bullet to make the API work explicit: "Build and maintain onboarding services and REST APIs and customer-facing flows using React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL and AWS in a six-person cross-functional team." Only retain "REST APIs" if these services are in fact REST-based, as the source material lists REST as an experienced backend technology.
3. In the Älvgrind experience section, strengthen the operational-reliability evidence by revising the on-call bullet to: "Participate in an on-call rota one week every six weeks, using Sentry and Datadog when investigating production issues." Keep this wording only for the investigation activity supported by actual experience; do not add claims about post-mortems or incident-management processes that are not in the candidate information.
5. In the Professional Summary, retain the honest Python qualification but make the comparable-language positioning more immediately visible. For example: "Backend and full-stack engineer with 10+ years of professional web development experience, including production backend services in Node.js, TypeScript, NestJS and Express." Keep the existing sentence that Python experience is limited to personal Home Assistant integrations; do not imply professional Python experience or willingness to work mainly in Python that the candidate has not stated.
